question: How general is the dissociation between signal displacement, amplitude propagation, and relative-phase reconfiguration across perturbation sign, strength, duration, connectivity-defined target centrality, matched A/B target set, and gain regime?

rules.association: Spearman correlation within each factor level, pooling only the remaining balanced factors and seeds
rules.localization_support: localization contrast greater than zero in at least 95 percent of pairs within a factor level
rules.factor_effects: report median and paired seed-matched differences for each measurement; do not interpret scale differences across metrics as comparable effect sizes
rules.multiple_testing: descriptive exploratory analysis; report all prespecified levels and do not select by p-value

decision_labels.general: both phase-displacement and phase-propagation absolute rho remain below 0.8 and localization support passes for every level of sign, strength, duration, centrality, and A/B target
decision_labels.conditional: one or more prespecified perturbation levels fail those conditions while others pass
decision_labels.not_supported: most perturbation levels show strong coupling or fail localization

scope_limits: focality is fixed at ten regions and is not tested
anatomical target means connectivity-defined central/peripheral sets, not named functional systems
gain-regime strata are reported but do not define generality across perturbation families
this analysis reuses exploratory diagnostic data
